name: Normal-Guided Gaussian Splitting
definition: A strategy to determine the initial position of a newly split child Gaussian ($G_c$) by projecting a randomly sampled position onto the tangent plane of the parent Gaussian ($G_a$), guided by the parent's normal and the image gradient at the child's projected location.
summary: Normal-Guided Gaussian Splitting is a densification strategy that projects candidate positions onto a parent Gaussian's tangent plane weighted by image gradients, avoiding errors from unreliable depth priors.
